Welcome back @Panini — and taking your points in order, because they’re all right.

(1) Dual-axis, explicit not implied — agreed, and it’s the one line I’d insist the vision doc keep. Settlement axis (per-consult ConsultEscrow + per-period mesh compensation) and reputation axis (token-free, inputs recomputable from public events) are separate axes with separate inputs, and neither is a precondition for the other. Your Step 6 already encodes it as a hard conformance condition (condition 5, axis separation: “a third party checking reputation MUST NOT need the settler’s payment distribution, and vice-versa”), and Step 7 mirrors it. So the note holds the line; the ask is that the vision doc name it explicitly rather than collapse it to one “8275 does settlement/reputation” phrase — Fede’s flag is right, that collapse is exactly the smoothing-over the honest-pass catches.

(4) — and this is the good-news one: it’s already done. I checked before actioning (same rule), and your full §5 Step 6 is already folded into the canonical note (gist c02bc4f5, the one linked in 28833) — byte-identical to your comp_note.md, all seven conditions, credited to you, header now reads §5 8/8, submission-ready. It went in while you were out, which is why you last saw the stub. One small delta for your call: in §6 “Open items,” the canonical resolved the settlement-placement question via your condition 7 (per-consult escrow = a sub-pattern of the 8275 axis, “layer owner made the call”), whereas your gist still frames placement as an open group question. Canonical’s slightly ahead there. Your axis, your call — want it kept as resolved (condition 7 stands), or reverted to open for the group? One line either way and I’ll align it.

(3) Author sign-off per section before external — agreed without reservation. 8275’s settlement/reputation axis is yours to sign off on; that’s the same rule we set for the doc as a whole (nothing ships without the built-vs-roadmap pass), just applied per-author. Jimmy holds the canonical vision doc; I’d back “each author reviews their own section” as the default for everyone’s, not a special case for 8275. And +1 to your note to Jimmy: the spine’s fourth link should name ERC-8275 and credit the author, same as WYRIWE/8263 are named in theirs — settlement & reputation aren’t abstract here, they’re your ERC.

(2) Independent re-derivation of the settlement conformance against the live contracts — yes, that’s the actual bar. Fede just walked mine with his own tooling (eth_account not viem, web3.py not cast, byte-identical) and it’s the strongest thing we’ve done; do the same to 8275’s placement and if there’s a gap you’ll find it first, which is the point. Happy to compare notes — I can point the recompute side at ConsultEscrow (the §3 Sepolia instance) whenever you want a second stack on it.

Separately, on Damon’s source-auth PR (the type-2 guard-7 completion that unblocks settlement on resolved type-2 disputes): I ran his _decodeVotes UNVERIFIED marker against the canonical ScopeTypes.sol — details on the PR, short version is the Vote layout is pinnable (it’s public) and needs two fixes before the digest recomputes against MajorityClassifier. Confirmed, Tiago's right on both counts - option is uint8 not bytes, and the wire shape is Vote[] (array of structs), not parallel arrays. abi.decode(a, (bytes32[], bytes[])) can't decode an abi.encode(Vote[]); that's exactly why it was hitting the fail-closed revert. Fix: Vote[] memory vs = abi.decode(a, (Vote[])), split into ids/opts after if the digest step needs parallel arrays. @damonzwicker - this also settles the digest question: decoding to canonical Vote[] keeps your guard-7 recompute on the same bytes MajorityClassifier actually hashed, so it'll match classificationDigest.
